newsitem.title: UK: UK's Offer sees 3 regions kicking off competition.
newsitem.headline: UK's Offer sees 3 regions kicking off competition.

text.p: UK electricity industry watchdog Offer said on Wednesday that it saw Eastern, Seeboard and Yorkshire Electricity opening up their markets to competition on April 1, 1998.
Other regional electricity companies (Recs) are expected to open up their markets between April and July as each completes integration and testing of new systems, a statement from Offer said.
The three specific areas within these regions are expected to be Norwich for Eastern, Canterbury for Seeboard and Hull for Yorkshire, Offer said.
"The market will open to competition in the attached postcode areas as soon as the relevant (Rec) has fully tested and robust systems in place," Offer head Stephen Littlechild said in a statement.
Offer laid out specific areas to be first in every region to open up to competition, amounting to around 10 percent of each region's total customers.
It said the exact dates for each region and the areas to be included in a second phase of liberalisation would be announced at a later date.
